title: Evolution of Cold-Sprayed Copper Deposit Mechanical Properties as Function of Substrate Geometry and Heat Treatment Parameters
InformationInFigures: Yes. Microstructure/grain size of as-sprayed deposits (Fig. 4). Elastic modulus in stress-strain curves (Fig. 7)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Storage_Condition: in an inert atmosphere in between spraying sessions
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: cleaned by grit-blasting (alumina grit 24). painted with Tremclad high heat enamel black paint from Rust-Oleum with 0.96 measured emissivity for temperature assessment.

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: Sprayed with 2 plates side-by-side. Top coat only. The deposit cross sections were cold vacuum mounted, ground, polished and etched using nitric acid (50 ml HNO3 + 50 ml H2O solution) for microstructural examination. Two tensile strain rates were used: 0.015 (up to 2 % strain) and 0.095 mm/mm/min (after 2 % strain)

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: DSC results do not show temperatures associated with recrystallization, indicating recrystallization has already occurred to a certain extent.  splat interfaces are largely composed of oxide films, oxide particles and small pores.

Experiments.Notes: AS SP-AL. Substrate composition (Steel vs. Al) did not result in significant changes in substrate temperature profile. Smaller substrates reached higher temps than larger substrates. The temperature of the center of deposits was measured, for this sample the min was 165°C and the max was 215°C. In this study, only SP-AL has achieved sufficiently high substrate temperature to show the onset of plastic deformation and some elongation

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Storage_Condition: in an inert atmosphere in between spraying sessions
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: cleaned by grit-blasting (alumina grit 24). painted with Tremclad high heat enamel black paint from Rust-Oleum with 0.96 measured emissivity for temperature assessment.

experimentalProperties.Deposition_Area_Dimensions: 75 mm x 75 mm x 5.0-5.3 mm thick
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: Two plates side by side during spraying. A laser-assisted bond layer was used to soften the steel, thereby maximizing deposit adhesion, followed by a top coat applied without laser assistance to achieve the required deposit thickness of 4-5 mm. All microstructures and properties come from the top coat. The deposit cross sections were cold vacuum mounted, ground, polished and etched using nitric acid (50 ml HNO3 + 50 ml H2O solution) for microstructural examination. Two tensile strain rates were used: 0.015 (up to 2 % strain) and 0.095 mm/mm/min (after 2 % strain)

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Box furnace HeaTechTM 4804-2 from Labline Instruments (Melrose Park, IL, USA) was used at 350°C. Samples were held at temperature for 1 h, and subsequently furnace cooled to ~ 60°C.
